gate: K9 gate 0: the barrier economics (measured first)

sync_survey.note: tl.extra.cuda exposes only the PDL utilities (gdc_wait/gdc_launch_dependents) and diagnostics; grid-wide sync inside one kernel is not expressible, and the NVIDIA launch path exposes no cooperative launch, so a software grid barrier cannot be made deadlock-safe by construction either

impossibility.verdict: the smem-resident distributed walk is impossible at the probe shape on this card: 256 CTAs of 64 KB do not fit 142 SMs (1 CTA/SM, 142 co-resident, 9.3 MB of addressable on-chip state < 16 MB of store), so no barrier -- cooperative or software -- can exist for it; and no grid-wide sync is Triton-expressible in any case. The store CAN wholly live on-chip in the L2 (16 MB < 96 MB); the distributed design is therefore built on the L2-resident store with the launch boundary (graph-captured) as the per-token barrier

barrier_economics.note: the per-token barrier of the Triton-expressible design is the kernel-launch boundary; eager it costs 10-19 us (2048 tokens x 3 x that is 65-118 ms/scan -- over budget), inside a whole-scan CUDA graph (the lane's K5B discipline) it is the graph node cost measured above

l2_streaming.note: the 16 MB store is L2-resident (96 MB L2): the distributed sweep reads it at the multi-CTA rate, the single-CTA fallback sweeps one 1 MB row at the single-CTA rate (latency-bound, the K7 fold class)

projection.fallback_note: the L2-resident single-CTA variant already exists: it is the K7 walk (receipts/k7_high_rank.json, 374.3 ms/scan at rank 2048, fold-bound at 275 GB/s effective); the distributed variant parallelises those folds across the slot-block CTAs

decision.rule: if 2048 tokens x syncs/token x measured barrier-us < 40 ms/scan then the distributed design, else the L2-resident single-CTA fallback
decision.variant: distributed walk, the store L2-resident on-chip, the per-token barrier the graph-captured launch boundary (the best Triton-expressible form of the distributed-persistent design; the smem-persistent form is impossible -- see impossibility)
decision.reason: the graph-captured launch boundary costs ~0.56 us/node, so 2048 tokens x 3 barriers = 3.4 ms/scan, under the 40 ms budget; the smem-resident form is receipted impossible (no Triton grid sync; 256 CTAs > 142 co-resident; 16 MB > 9.3 MB addressable on-chip), so the state rides the L2 -- on-chip at the probe shape -- and the sweeps distribute across CTAs exactly as the brief's design specifies
